name: Needle Drop Action Cue Timing
use_when: A music cue or drop can make a visual action, reveal, chase, product-placement beat, or section shift feel more stylish.
The track has a recognizable intro, pickup, downbeat, or escalation point.
The scene has a clear wide shot, impact, braking point, reveal, or action change to receive the cue.
A voiceover-led YouTube edit adds music early so some visual cuts can be shaped by beat.
A music cue needs shortening while preserving phrase, beat, or waveform continuity.
A speed-adjusted action clip needs its peak pose or impact aligned to a beat before transitions are added.
avoid_when: The strongest beat lands on a meaningless visual moment.
The scene needs realism, restraint, or quiet more than stylized energy.
Dialogue timing cannot survive the cue without being masked.
The edit starts cutting to every beat and loses story clarity.

timeline_pattern.cue_rule: Place the song's most satisfying cue on a meaningful story or action turn.
timeline_pattern.escalation_rule: When the visual action intensifies, the music should either escalate, drop out deliberately, or be replaced.
timeline_pattern.exit_rule: Plan the next dialogue or story beat before the music overwhelms it.
timeline_pattern.voiceover_rule: Use beat cuts only after the voiceover flow is understandable; music should support the edit's vibe, not force random cuts.
timeline_pattern.manual_splice_rule: When shortening music manually, cut on beats or similar waveform shapes and use a crossfade if the join is exposed.
timeline_pattern.clip_speed_rule: For AMV or action clips, adjust clip speed against beat markers until the action peak reaches the cue; do not rely on one universal speed value.

motion.rule: Use cuts, speed ramps, zooms, and wide-shot reveals only where they land with the cue and clarify the action.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: Aim for the action cut or motion accent to land within 1-2 frames of the intended beat for high-energy edits.
keyframe_values.pre_cue_length: Use enough intro or pickup for anticipation; trim if the pre-cue delays the visual payoff.
keyframe_values.escalation_marker: Mark the exact action change, brake, impact, or reveal that should receive the next musical lift.
keyframe_values.manual_crossfade: A short crossfade can hide a phrase splice when matching waveform peaks are close but not seamless.
keyframe_values.speed_match_sync: When speed-matching clips, preview at least the outgoing clip, synced clip, and next cut so the run feels musical.

sound.rule: Use beat markers, cue markers, and volume ducking so the drop feels intentional and dialogue remains clear.

captions.rule: Do not place captions over the key visual moment receiving the drop unless dialogue comprehension requires it.

color.rule: No required color rule; preserve action readability during music-led energy changes.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use waveform inspection and short exports around the cue. Trim audio start times and clip cuts so the drop aligns with the visual turn.
implementation.remotion: Represent beats as frame numbers and drive cuts or motion accents from cueFrame, dropFrame, escalationFrame, and exitFrame.
implementation.blender: Use audio markers for camera or object motion accents when the animation is tied to a track cue.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use beat markers, duplicate the section, and manually align the action cut or speed-adjusted action peak to the strongest cue rather than relying on auto-beat cuts.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Add markers on song cue, downbeat, action turn, escalation, duck, and exit; for voiceover-first edits, add early music markers after the VO trim and use them for selected asset cuts only.

common_mistakes: Dropping the strongest cue on a random shot.
Forcing every cut to the beat after the main cue lands.
Letting the track tempo fight the action pacing.
Forgetting to duck or exit before dialogue returns.
Using a cue that is fun but tonally wrong for the scene.
Forcing script-driven visuals onto beats where the spoken idea needs a different timing.
Using AI music retiming or a manual splice without listening for a musical bump.
Changing clip speed before marking the beat or choosing the exact action peak.
qc: Does the main cue land within 1-2 frames of the intended visual turn?
Can the editor name the story reason for the drop?
Does music escalation match the action escalation?
Is dialogue clear immediately after the cue?
Does the section avoid unnecessary beat-cutting after the payoff?
Do music-based cuts preserve voiceover comprehension and script logic?
If the track was shortened, does the splice land on a beat, phrase, or matching waveform shape without a distracting bump?
If clip speed was changed, does the action peak still read clearly while landing on the intended beat?
